story_lines.text: I'm a senior product manager.
Ten years in product in total, the last six in logistics software.
Before that I was a business analyst for about two years at a bank's operations team.
Right now I'm at a company I'll call FleetGrid.
It's a mid-size SaaS company that sells dispatch and tracking software to regional trucking firms.
I joined in March 2021 as a product manager and became senior product manager in April 2023.
My area is the carrier app and the exceptions desk.
The exceptions desk is where dispatchers handle the loads that go wrong, like a late pickup, a wrong address or a damaged shipment.
The biggest thing I shipped is an AI triage feature for that exceptions desk.
Every exception that came in got a suggested category and a suggested next step.
Before that, dispatchers read every ticket from scratch.
I didn't write the model.
Our ML engineer, two backend engineers and one designer built it with me.
I wrote the spec, I set up the evaluation, and I ran the pilot.
The evaluation was the part I cared about most.
We took 400 past exceptions that dispatchers had already closed, and two senior dispatchers labelled the right category for each one.
That was our test set, and nobody was allowed to tune the prompt on it.
The first version got 71 percent of categories right on that set.
That was not good enough to ship, because a wrong category sends the ticket to the wrong team.
We changed it so that it only suggested a category when it was confident, and otherwise it said "needs a human".
On the cases where it did suggest, it was right 92 percent of the time, and it suggested on about 64 percent of tickets.
We piloted it with three customers for six weeks.
Median time to the first action on an exception went from about 19 minutes to about 11 minutes across those three customers.
I want to be careful here, it was three customers, so it is a pilot number, not a company-wide number.
One thing went wrong in the pilot.
The model started tagging every weather delay as a "carrier fault", because one customer typed weather notes in the carrier field.
We caught it because I had asked for a weekly sample review of 30 suggestions.
We fixed the input mapping, not the model.
My lesson from that is that a weekly human review of a small sample is cheaper than any dashboard, and it catches the strange failures.
The second thing I'd talk about is a failed launch.
In 2022 we built a self-serve onboarding flow for small carriers.
I pushed for it.
Sign-ups went up but almost none of those carriers became paying accounts in the first quarter.
About 4 percent converted.
What I learned is that small carriers didn't want self-serve, they wanted a phone call.
We kept the flow for lead capture and put a sales call behind it.
I would not call that launch a success, and I say so when people ask.
I lead without being anyone's manager.
I work with one engineering manager, and my team is about seven engineers, one designer and a part-time data analyst.
Stakeholders I work with most are the head of customer success and the VP of product.
I send a written weekly update every Friday, one page, with what shipped, what slipped and why.
I took a career break from June 2019 to February 2020, about eight months.
My father had heart surgery and I was the one at home to look after him.
During that time I did an online course in SQL and product analytics, and I finished it.
When I came back I joined a smaller logistics startup as a product manager for about a year, then moved to FleetGrid.
I've never had a referral for any of my jobs.
Every role I got was through a cold application or a recruiter message.
I find asking for referrals uncomfortable, because I don't like asking people I don't know well.
Why I'm looking now: FleetGrid is moving my area into maintenance mode and I want to keep working on applied AI in operations software.
What I want next is a senior PM role where AI is in the core workflow, and the team actually measures whether it works.
Tools I use day to day: Jira, Figma for reviewing designs, Amplitude for product data, and SQL on our warehouse.
I can write basic SQL queries myself.
I don't write production code.
I'm based in Pune and I'm open to remote roles or to hybrid in Pune.
On the triage evaluation, the 400 cases were from the previous four months of closed exceptions, and we removed duplicates first.
The two dispatchers disagreed on about 1 in 10 cases.
For those, the dispatch lead made the final call.
I wrote that down as our tie-break rule before we started.
I have not built an evaluation for a generative model, only for classification.
If someone asks, I say that plainly.
The 19 to 11 minutes number is the median, not the average.
The average moved less, because a few very long cases stayed long.
I have never managed people directly.
I mentored one associate product manager for about a year.
I speak English, Hindi and Marathi.
I write product documents in English.

That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it.
We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people.
Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world.
We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people.
Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment?
Come join us. ## **The opportunity:** We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join Flexport's product team and own a critical part of how we serve clients and operators across global logistics.

You'll define the vision and roadmap for your product area, ship features that drive measurable business outcomes, and collaborate with engineering, design, commercial, and operations teams to solve hard problems at scale.
Flexport's platform powers every stage of global freight, from booking and pricing to visibility, customs, and delivery.
The products you build will be used daily by logistics managers, supply chain leaders, freight operators, and internal teams who keep goods moving around the world.

This is a high-impact role for someone who combines strong product instincts with deep analytical skills and comfort navigating complex domains. ## The team: The **Commerce** team owns the end-to-end quality, automation, and profitability of Flexport’s commerce domain.

We build intelligent agents to automate critical commerce workflows, including quoting, billing, and invoicing, while driving cost intelligence across every shipment process gate to optimize profitability.

Additionally, our team expands the marketplace catalog for new offerings and develops next-generation, client-facing commerce products and payments technology. ## **You will:** ## **You should have:** #LI-onsite #LI-VA1 The US base salary range for this position (this does not include bonus, equity and benefits): $174,000 - $213,000 USD #### Commitment to Equal Opportunity At Flexport, our ability to fulfill our mission of making global commerce easy and accessible relies on having a diverse, dedicated and engaged workforce.

Feb 24, 2025, 11:54 ET ## Share this article Share toX Share this article Share toX At the forefront of the launch are Flexport Intelligence with an AI Insights Builder, and Flexport Control Tower expanding supply chain visibility and management capabilities. [...] SAN FRANCISCO, Feb.

24, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Flexport, the global leader in supply chain technology, today announced its first Winter Release, launching more than 20 tech and AI-powered products designed to transform global logistics.
The highlight of the release is Flexport Intelligence, which allows businesses to ask questions in natural language and receive immediate insights about their supply chain performance.

Flexport customers can use this AI-powered tool to build reports and create dashboards with no technical skills required, making it extremely easy for operations managers to take control of their global supply chains.

Continue Reading [...] Internal Technology to Deliver the Highest Quality and Best Value for ClientsIn this release, Flexport is sharing an inside look at the powerful technology that enables its operations teams to provide unmatched quality, service, and lower costs for customers.

From route optimization and workflow automation to customs compliance tools, the company is sharing a look under the hood at how it builds technology to coordinate complexity and simplify the world of global logistics.
"Flexport's technology isn't just about automation—it's about augmentation," said Sanne Manders, President of Flexport.
"Our tools free up human ingenuity to tackle challenges AI alone can't solve, delivering the highest quality service at the best value."
The expansion represents the first international rollout of Flexport’s fulfillment business and extends its end-to-end logistics network into two markets where many of its customers already sell.

Flexport said customers can now import inventory in bulk, store products domestically and fulfill orders within each country while continuing to use the same Flexport platform, account team and freight and customs relationships. “Our customers built demand in Canada and the UK long before they had a good way to serve it,” Flexport founder and CEO Ryan Petersen said in a statement. “Flexport customers using freight through fulfillment in the U.S. have seen tangible efficiencies and cost savings with end-to-end logistics.” ## Flexport targets Toronto, Manchester
